chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: Hiring jazz arranger John Bartee; Mario as musician of musicians
summary: Mario hired jazz arrangers like Bartee, who loved Debussy, to bring legato lines and counterpoint into an Afro-Cuban band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I notice he didn't have no Cuban, Puerto Rican or Latin music arranger. He got the best in jazz, John Bartee. John Bartee, I believe, was working with Fletcher Henderson at times.
Why did he pick John Bartee? Did he want that sound?
Because Bartee has, he was in love with Debussy, and Mario........

......and he has so many good qualities in music, he was practically different than everyone. Maybe he wasn't the best, but he had something that he ahh - was familiar with what we liked. All legato things, all the counterpoints,

contra-motion, all those beautiful things; because Mario, in account that it was our band, he want to imply, he want to put in the band where, what he think music was calling for. So that's why Mario is different practically than any musician that I know.
That's right, because no one else would have ever thought of hiring ......
.....a black jazz musician to be the arranger of an Afro-Cuban band.

He is a musician of musicians. Maybe, you know, it is very hard to ---I know I have a limitation in education, it's very hard to listen to an intellectual when he talking to intellectuals. To a mediocre education cannot understand what they are talking about. If you go to the United Nations and you don't have the proper education, you go, but there you think that they are kidding, they playing around, they play a lot of nonsense, because you are not prepared to be there.
